newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks close softer, evade Dow's drop.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks close softer, evade Dow's drop.

text.p: Toronto's key stock index closed slightly lower in heavy dealings on Wednesday but avoided the 120-point tumble in New York as commodity stocks strengthened.

The Toronto Stock Exchange's 300 Composite Index slipped 6.23 points to 6574.61 in brisk turnover. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped almost 120 points to 7842 after coming within striking distance of the watershed 8000 level.
"The real shift is to commodities, which will help Toronto over the next few quarters," said Michael Metz, Oppenheimer & Co. Inc.'s chief investment strategist.
Metz has predicted that Toronto would extend its recent rally amid a global industrial boom that would benefit its heavyweight natural resource groups.
Gold bullion prices resumed their dive after Tuesday's marginal bounce, pressuring Toronto's influential gold sector. The key Comex price slipped $2.10 to reach $318.90, near 12-year lows again.
But "even though gold was down, there were still a couple of bright spots," a trader said.
They included six of Toronto's 14 sub-sectors, which added points. Forestry products, industrial products and utilities led the way.
Conglomerates, consumer products and media weakened along with golds.
Trading was heavy at 109 million shares worth C$1.8 billion ($1.3 billion). Declining issues outpaced advances 583 to 424, with 295 ending flat.
Steelmaker IPSCO Inc. rose 2.20 to 44 after announcing details of a large pipe order totalling 180,000 tons.
IPL Energy Inc. rose 1.55 to 49.40 in moderate trade as investors approved of its purchase of a 32 percent stake in Quebec holding company Noverco Inc.

Battered paper maker Repap Enterprises Inc. rose 0.12 to 0.50 in trading of more than 3.7 million shares. It agreed on Wednesday to sell its Repap USA unit to Consolidated Papers Inc. for $674 million.
